sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in New Jersey, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Tuesday, October 27Passed

To have your ballot mailed to you, your application must reach your County Clerk not less than 7 days before the election: by Tuesday, October 27, 2026. After that you can still apply in person at your County Clerk's office until 3 p.m. on Monday, November 2, 2026. (official page)

Send it back

A mailed ballot must be postmarked on or before Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and reach your county Board of Elections by Monday, November 9, 2026 (six days after the polls close). A ballot with no postmark counts if the Postal Service delivers it by Thursday, November 5. A ballot put in a drop box or handed in at the Board of Elections must be in by 8 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Sunday, November 1, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on New Jersey’s own site

At school away from home, in New Jersey or in another state? What New Jersey says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed. Every active registered voter can ask for a mail-in ballot (New Jersey's name for an absentee ballot). The state says the law allows a mail-in ballot "for any reason". Some voters already get one for every election (the state says to ask your County Clerk how to stop that); others must apply. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Apply on the state's Vote-By-Mail online application. You need your date of birth and a New Jersey driver's license or non-driver ID number; if you use your Social Security number instead, you must be able to sign on screen or upload your signature. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Print your county's Application for Mail-in Ballot (English, Spanish and other languages), sign it, and mail it to your County Clerk. Open it (official page)
  • In person. Apply in person at your County Clerk's office and pick up your mail-in ballot there, until 3 p.m. on Monday, November 2, 2026. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it a few days before Election Day, or ask a clerk at a post office counter to hand-stamp the postmark. Whether you need a stamp depends on your county; ask your County Clerk. (official page)
  • Drop box. Put it in one of your county's secure ballot drop boxes by 8 p.m. on Election Day. The state's website lists every county's drop boxes. (official page)
  • In person. Hand it in at your county Board of Elections office by 8 p.m. on Election Day. You may NOT bring it to an early voting site or your polling place. Someone else may carry it for you as a "bearer": they must sign the bearer part of the outer envelope in front of you, and show ID and sign the bearer book if they hand it in. A bearer may carry no more than three ballots of people outside their household (up to five in all if the others are family living with them). (official page)

What the envelope needs

No witness or notary is needed. Fill in and sign the certificate attached to the inner envelope, and keep it attached; do not put it inside the envelope. You do not need to send a copy of your ID, except some first-time voters, who will get a notice about it with their ballot. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on New Jersey’s own site

Use the state's Track My Ballot portal. The first time, you create an account using your voter ID number, driver's license number or the last four digits of your Social Security number. (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Saturday, October 24, 2026 to Sunday, November 1, 2026.

Early voting on machines runs Saturday, October 24 through Sunday, November 1, 2026, at your county's early voting sites, at least 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. Monday to Saturday and 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Sunday. If you are signed up to vote by mail for this election, you must first opt out with your County Clerk to vote on a machine. (official page)

Students

At school in New Jersey, away from home

New Jersey's Division of Elections says a college student can register from their college address or their parent's address, and "the final choice is yours". To vote in New Jersey you must have lived in the county for 30 days before the election. A student registered at home can apply for a mail-in ballot to vote while away at school. (official page)

At school in another state, with New Jersey as home

The state's pages do not speak to students in other states separately. Its student page says college students may register from their college address or their parent's address, and suggests a mail-in ballot as a way to vote "at home or away at school". A student who keeps their New Jersey registration can apply for a mail-in ballot to be sent to them. (official page)

Military and overseas

Military and overseas voters register by Tuesday, October 13, 2026 and ask for a ballot with the Federal Post Card Application: by mail by Tuesday, October 27, or by email or fax by Friday, October 30, 2026. You can send your voted ballot by mail, email or fax, but if you email or fax it you must also mail the paper ballot right away. It must be postmarked by Election Day and received by Monday, November 9, 2026. (federal guide)

New Jersey in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • New Jersey calls absentee ballots "mail-in" or "vote-by-mail" ballots.
  • If you got a mail-in ballot and go to your polling place on Election Day instead, you will vote on a paper provisional ballot, not a machine.
  • If you make a mistake on, damage or lose your mail-in ballot and have not returned it, ask your County Clerk for a replacement.
  • Voting questions: the state's hotline is 1-877-NJ-VOTER (1-877-658-6837).
